title: Understanding the Anesthesiologist Assistant Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion for a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert an anesthesiologist assistant salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, with tax, super, and award rate context from Fair Work and the ATO.
salarySummary: An anesthesiologist assistant salary is not set by a single award, but using the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week gives an annual gross of $52,285.44, while actual rates are typically much higher under enterprise agreements or health professional awards.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for an anesthesiologist assistant in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single award rate for anesthesiologist assistants in the Fair Work Ombudsman's Nurses Award or the Modern Awards Pay Database. Most anesthesiologist assistants are covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020 or an enterprise agreement, with hourly rates often ranging from $35 to $55 per hour depending on experience and location. For a precise figure, check your specific award or agreement.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly rate for a 38-hour week?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week, then by 52 weeks. For example, at $40 per hour: $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 gross per year. Fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2 (e.g., $1,520 × 2 = $3,040). This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick estimates.

faqs.q: Does the anesthesiologist assistant salary include superannuation and casual loading?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your base salary at 12% of ordinary earnings (up to the $270,830 contribution base). Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate instead of paid leave. For example, a casual anesthesiologist assistant on $40/hour would get $50/hour including loading. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Anesthesiologist Assistant Salary to Annual Pay

When you're offered an hourly rate as an anesthesiologist assistant, understanding your annual salary is essential for budgeting, tax planning, and comparing job offers. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, using the latest Fair Work Ombudsman and Australian Taxation Office data.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross salary is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks**

For example, if your anesthesiologist assistant salary is $45 per hour:
- Weekly pay: $45 × 38 = $1,710
- Fortnightly pay: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420
- Annual gross: $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920

This formula assumes you work the same 38 hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for your [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimate.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets minimum pay rates through modern awards. For anesthesiologist assistants, the relevant award is often the *Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020*, though some roles fall under enterprise agreements. As a baseline, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

To see how award rates are structured, look at the Nurses Award 2020 as an example. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide shows a registered nurse level 1, pay point 1 earns $32.09 per hour, with higher rates for Saturday ($48.14), Sunday ($56.16), and public holidays ($64.18). Anesthesiologist assistants typically earn above these nurse rates due to specialised training.

### Using the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database

The Fair Work Commission publishes a Modern Awards Pay Database updated after each Annual Wage Review. The 2026 data (last updated 1 October 2026) includes classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. While the database doesn't list an 'anesthesiologist assistant' classification, you can find the relevant health professional award and check your pay point. Always refer to your specific award or enterprise agreement for accurate rates.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual anesthesiologist assistant, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading in lieu of paid leave. For example, a base rate of $40 per hour becomes $50 per hour casual. This loading is applied before penalty rates. Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you toggle casual loading with a checkbox—never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). The Australian Taxation Office sets a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year for the super guarantee. So if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer contributes $12,000 to super, making your total remuneration $112,000. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Tax on Your Anesthesiologist Assistant Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a $88,920 annual salary, the estimated tax is about $17,577 plus Medicare $1,778, leaving a take-home of approximately $69,565 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed breakdown.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Most employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply weekly pay × 2. For a $45/hour rate: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420. After tax and Medicare, you might receive around $2,675 per fortnight. This helps with budgeting for rent, bills, and savings.

### What About Average Earnings?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' May 2026 Average Weekly Earnings report shows full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. Anesthesiologist assistants often earn above the national average due to demand and skill level, but actual salaries vary by state, employer, and experience.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay estimates here are hourly rate × hours per week × 52. They assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised calculations, refer to your employment contract, check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) page, or use the [reference tables](/data) for award rates. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest national figures, and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) compares your salary to industry benchmarks.
